steps.text: In a bowl beat butter or margarine until fluffy. Gradually add 2 cups of the confectioners’ sugar, beating well.
Slowly beat in the milk and vanilla. Slowly beat in remaining sugar. Beat in additional milk, if needed, to make of spreading consistency. Tint with food color, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Butter Frosting
raw_recipe.description: Plenty of butter makes this rich frosting that goes great on any cookie.

review.reviewBody: Great frosting. i used it on top of chocolate cupcakes and it was fantastic. I tinted all different colours and it mixed really well. It was a bit too stiff to work with so i put it in the microwave for 15 seconds and it was slightly more creamy. It holds its shape really well. So tasty!

Made it per instructions with the exceptions of doubling the butter and I also used 1/2 a vanilla bean and heated it in the milk. Afterwards I let it cool and scraped bean out. It gave the icing a nice authentic vanilla flavor.

Great buttery flavor and texture. Yes, it is sweet which is what I expect for frosting. I tried the receipe twice. I reduced the sugar to 4 cups because I was using it on a cake. It was still too stiff, so I microwaved it for 45 seconds to get it to spread nicely. The second time, I melted the butter and stuck to 4 cups sugar. Turned out great.

I changed this recipe so much that I am not sure it is even the same recipe, but I loved the way I made it. So here it is: 4 cups powdered sugar. 1/3 cup milk. 1 stick melted butter. 1/2 large lemon juiced. Mix together starting with butter then alternating liquids. It was thin, but zingy and yum, yum, yummy.

These are the exact ingredients my grandma taught me how to use! I didn't even know a recipe was needed. We always just eyeballed the ingredients. If it was too wet we added more powdered sugar, too sugary and we added a little more butter, and if too thick we added more milk about a teaspoon at a time. I don't think that it is the best frosting, as it is so super sweet, but it is a very simple frosting that even a kid can make. Cocoa can also be added to make a chocolate version. Although, this frosting will not harden up like a royal or cookie icing, unless the cookies are froze! So, don't plan on using if you're trying to make fancy cookies to take some where and need a hard type icing.

This was so easy!! My cousin and I made this at 2 am to frost a lemon cake. We added lemon extract and yellow food coloring to the frosting, and it was really good! Just make sure you put in enough of the powdered sugar, or it will get a bit runny and drip out the sides of the cake... Still tastes good, but looks kinda weird! Also, I'd recommend sifting the sugar before putting it in the frosting. We didn't do this because we didn't have a sieve handy, but I think it would have eliminated the somewhat gritty texture (that's why I gave it 4 stars).

I found a bundt cake on this web site ("Too much chocolate cake"), try it, it is SO moist, I'll never try another, the recipe is the bomb. I do a different flavor cake and icing each time I make it. This time I made a Cherry Chip cake. I usually "doctor" up canned frosting to enhance the cake. I had no canned frosting so off to Allrecipes I went. All the recipes called for crisco, and or flour, I didn't want to use those. Then I came across this one. Very simple ingredients, I substituted Almond extract for the vanilla extract. Oh my, I have used this combination of ingredients many times for frosting and the frosting NEVER tasted like this. It must be the order in which you mix this. It is light and heavenly. The almond flavor went beautifully with the cherry chip cake. I will never doctor up canned frosting again. This is the one!

Excellent! Added additional sugar to make stiffer for a frosting gun. Need to let it sit up a bit before you use. I put on cooled cupcakes, but the frosting ran on the first ones. By the time I did the last one though, it was setting nicely.

I had never made frosting before and wanted to make home made frosting for my daughter's birthday party. I found that you don't really need to sift the confectionery sugar. I made a batch with milk as directed above and then made another batch with half and half. The consensus around our house was both were good but we preferred the half and half version. It was a little smoother and not so sweet. I also only used 1 teaspoon of vanilla. With those little tweaks, I thought it was perfect. I have been eating left over cupcakes just so I can eat up all the frosting all week.

Very good! I used a teaspoon of vanilla and 1/2 teaspoon of almond extract instead of 1-1/2 teaspoons of vanilla. I didn't use the entire amount of powdered sugar - just kept adding until I got the consistency I wanted. It was the perfect amount for one batch of my sugar cookies.
It tasted ok, but it was far too thin with the 1/4 c. milk. I recommend using 2 Tbsp.
I use this recipe for almost EVERYTHING!!!!!!!
Wonderful buttery taste and makes more than enough for a two layer cake. Thank you Desiree.
Easy to make and tastes great! This recipe makes a lot more than the containers of frosting you buy in the store and it tastes a lot better!
EXCELLENT recipe!!
too sweet. 4 CUPS OF SUGAR, TOO MUCH!!!
All together it was fairly nice. A little thick for me but however I did not follow the recipe exactly so I can't be 100% sure. :)
Delicious!! Followed the recipe exactly and turned out perfect. Easy to make and so much better than the pre-made frosting in the can.
Fanstic frosting for cookies! The whole family loved it. My son was able to make this one too.
So easy and so good
